title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: Existing GNNs construct their feature space by repeatedly multiplying node attributes with structure matrices (or structure polynomials), and the paper shows theoretically and empirically that these feature subspaces become asymptotically linearly correlated, so weight sharing and limited node-attribute dimensionality bound the representable space. Motivated by this, the paper proposes FE-GNN, which (1) flattens the feature subspaces by reweighting every subspace independently and (2) adds structural principal components (a truncated SVD of the graph structure) as an extra, orthogonal feature subspace, with column-wise normalization and a purely linear implementation. On random 60/20/20 splits over 100 runs, FE-GNN reaches 73.33% on Chameleon and 67.82% on Squirrel (vs 61.85% and 47.21% for GCN), an average 32.0% improvement over GCN on three heterophilic datasets and a 1.1% average gain over ADA-UGNN on five homophilic datasets, at comparable per-epoch training time.

match_target.why: The user hint points at Table 2, FE-GNN (C) on Chameleon, and this is the cheapest claim that still shows the paper's central result: Chameleon is the smallest heterophilic dataset (2,277 nodes, 128 features) with a ~62 ms SVD and <1 min per run, and its 11.8-point gain over the w/o S ablation (plus the 11.5-point gain over GCN) is the clearest evidence for the structural-principal-components modification, i.e. the headline 32% heterophilic improvement.

tolerance.why: Rule 1 applies: Table 2 reports a spread for the exact target value (FE-GNN (C), Chameleon, 73.33±0.35) from repeated runs (100 runs on 10 random seeds, printed as a 95% confidence interval). Taking the reported spread as the band, 3 × 0.35 = 1.05, rounded up to the two decimals the paper prints. (Rule 2 does not apply because the 20% Chameleon test split is only ~455 nodes; rule 3's 2.0-point cap for bounded accuracies would also be satisfied but is looser than the paper's own reported uncertainty.)

requirements.stmt: Represent a GNN as a sum over T non-parametric feature subspaces reweighted by parameters, H = sum_t Phi_t(X, A_hat) Theta_t, so that feature space and weights can be separated.
requirements.quote: the non-parametric feature space constructing function that inputs the graph data

requirements.stmt: FE-GNN must build the feature space in two ways: polynomial feature subspaces Pk(L_hat)X and an additional subspace S of structural principal components, H = sum_k Pk(L_hat)X W^(k) + S Ws.
requirements.quote: we use the principal components of the structural matrices to form another feature subspace S

requirements.stmt: Each feature subspace must be reweighted by its own independent parameter matrix (flattening), not a shared weight matrix.
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses independent parameter matrices W (k) and Ws to reweight each feature subspace

requirements.stmt: Apply column-wise normalization so that every column of every feature subspace has equal scale in the concatenated feature space.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally to the whole feature space

requirements.stmt: The model itself must be purely linear: no activation functions and no dropout, only the cross-entropy loss (non-linearity is only allowed in the baselines).
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: Build the structural subspace S from the truncated SVD of the graph structure matrix (principal components and their singular values) and keep S fixed; only Ws is learned.
requirements.quote: we extract the low-dimensional information for the graph structure to obtain its principal components

requirements.stmt: Choose the truncation so that about 94% of the cumulative singular values are kept (|S| = the suggested whole hundred of components).
Use random 60%/20%/20% train/validation/test splits and average over 100 runs (10 random seeds) for every reported number.
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs in Table 2

requirements.stmt: Report average accuracy (equivalent to micro-F1 for single-label classification) with a 95% confidence interval.
requirements.quote: We report the average accuracy (micro F1 score) in the classification task with a 95% confidence interval in all the tables and figures.

requirements.stmt: Optimize with Adam and early stopping with a warmup of 50 epochs and patience 200.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200

requirements.stmt: Use the FE-GNN hyper-parameters of Table 8 per dataset (Chameleon: lr 0.01, weight decay 0.0005, |S|=700, hidden 64, k=3) and the stated grid search otherwise (lr {0.01,0.05,0.1}; weight decay {0.0005,...,0.05}; |S| grids; k in {0,1,2,3}).
requirements.quote: Suggested |S|: the whole hundred from the 94% singular values

requirements.stmt: Treat all datasets as undirected graphs, as assumed in the preliminaries.
requirements.quote: We set these datasets to undirected graphs as we assumed in the Preliminaries.

requirements.stmt: Use polynomial order around K=3 (with the Chebyshev variant for FE-GNN (C)), deeper orders giving only marginal changes.
requirements.quote: This suggests that order 3 is good enough to achieve near-optimal performance
